newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM predicts 4-5 pct '97 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM predicts 4-5 pct '97 GDP growth.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius said on Monday that the growth of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 would between four and five percent and forecast yearly inflation of 16 percent.
Stankevicius, speaking before a cabinet meeting where the 1997 budget will be considered, said the government had tried but failed to draw up a deficit-free budget.
"We tried to make it a non-deficit budget but the draft has a deficit. However, we will try to reduce it to 1.75 percent of GDP," he told a news conference.
The 1996 budget was planned with a deficit of around 700 million litas, more than two percent of GDP but within International Monetary Fund (IMF) guidelines.
Inflation this year was running at 22.3 percent on a year-on-year basis in September while the economy is expected to grow between one and two percent.
Stankevicius' Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) is expected to be defeated at elections, the first round of which takes place on October 20.
